properties.name: WHAT WORKED, re-measured on 0.77.0 (2026-10-02): the door's exit codes, `--args -` from stdin and RUST_LOG=error quieting hold, and graph_report takes ~0.2 s at 110 nodes. Two corrections. The 0.2 s does not hold at real size (reflow2's own 6,309-node design: graph_report ~7.9 s, get_node ~1.0 s). A missing argument gives exit 2 only when the tool's schema requires it; a field required only to CREATE gives exit 1. Do not regress either half
properties.statement:
From the "What works" and "Measured" sections of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, re-measured by triage agent D: reflow2-mcp 0.77.0 release binary, isolated HOME, scratch stores. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-D/measure.log; outputs in triage-D/out/.

ROWS COVERED, report's claim then this measurement:
1. "--call graph_report on a scratch graph: about 0.2 s per call, including opening the store." HOLDS AT SMALL SIZE: an empty store 0.09–0.12 s (5 runs); a hand-built 110-node/140-edge design 0.18–0.21 s (5 runs). DOES NOT HOLD AT REAL SIZE: main's export (6,309 nodes, 41,546 edges) imported into a scratch store gives graph_report 7.9–9.9 s (5 runs), loop_status 7.7–9.0 s, and get_node 0.96–1.09 s. That get_node figure is roughly the floor for opening a store that size. Every door call pays the open, which a long-lived MCP session pays once. An instructions file that says "calls are cheap" is true for a small design only.
2. Exit codes: 0 is a reply on stdout; 1 is a refusal on stderr ("reflow2: `tool` refused — ..."); 2 is a reply the tool marked is_error, on STDOUT as a JSON string. All HOLD. Exit 1 also carries the CLI's own errors, e.g. "Error: --args is not JSON ..." for bad JSON.
3. "A write with a missing argument → exit 2; the message names the missing argument." PARTLY. Schema-required arguments give exit 2 with the argument named on stdout: create_edges without `edges`, and record_finding without `subject_id` (that reply also lists every required argument). Fields required only to CREATE give exit 1 with a refusal on stderr that names them: add_requirement without `statement`, and add_capability without `name`/`description`. Both name the argument. The exit code depends on which layer refused, so an agent keyed on "2 = missing argument" misreads half the cases.
4. "`--args -` reads the object from stdin." HOLDS, byte-exact for apostrophes, double quotes, non-ASCII, $ and backticks under a quoted heredoc. Detail in fact:root-cause-door-prose-passes-two-quoting-layers-and-args-stdin-removes-the-shells-only-with-a-quoted-delimiter-2026-10-02.
5. "RUST_LOG=error hides the per-call INFO line and the WARN line a refusal adds." HOLDS. Unset: "INFO reflow2_mcp: opening reflow2 design graph" on every call, plus "WARN rmcp::service: response error ..." on a refusal. RUST_LOG=warn: the WARN line only. RUST_LOG=error: neither, and the refusal line stays.

Same capability, earlier "what worked": fact:worked-call-and-graph-path-made-isolated-measurements-possible-2026-09-29. This triage again ran every measurement through --call with --graph-path and a scratch HOME.
